"""Tests for uploads.validation."""

import pytest

from uploads import UploadRejected, validate_upload


def test_a_small_upload_is_accepted():
    """An upload under the size limit is returned unchanged."""
    assert validate_upload("report.pdf", 1024) == "report.pdf"


def test_an_oversized_upload_is_rejected():
    """An upload over the size limit is refused."""
    with pytest.raises(UploadRejected, match="too large"):
        validate_upload("report.pdf", 50 * 1024 * 1024)

content.text:
Implemented the three new validation rules in `src/uploads/validation.py`: reject filenames with a `/` or `\` path separator or a leading dot (instead of repairing), require the extension (case-insensitive) to be one of pdf/png/csv, and return the filename lowercased as the stored name — each with its own `UploadRejected` message. Removed the now-unused `base_name` repair helper from `naming.py` and added tests covering all the new cases.

`uv run pytest` (11 passed) and `uv run ruff check .` (all checks passed) both succeed. Note: `uv run ty check` errors, but only on an unrelated file (`scripts/check_skills.py`) outside this project because module resolution walks up to a parent git repo in this environment — pre-existing and unrelated to this change; the README only documents `pytest` as the check to run.
